definitions.explanation: The sale of goods in large quantities, typically to retailers rather than directly to consumers.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}は{卸売|おろしう}り{専門|せんもん}だ。
{卸売|おろしう}り{価格|かかく}で{買|か}えるので{安|やす}い。
examples.english: It's cheap because you can buy at wholesale prices.

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}は{築地|つきじ}の{卸売|おろしう}り{市場|しじょう}で{長年|ながねん}{働|はたら}いている。
examples.english: My father has worked at the Tsukiji wholesale market for many years.

notes:
USAGE:
Contrasts with {小売|こう}り (retail). Often seen in compound forms like {卸売|おろしう}り{市場|しじょう} (wholesale market) and {卸売|おろしう}り{業者|ぎょうしゃ} (wholesaler).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {卸売|おろしう}り{市場|しじょう} (wholesale market)
- {卸売|おろしう}り{価格|かかく} (wholesale price)
- {卸売|おろしう}り{業者|ぎょうしゃ} (wholesaler)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {小売|こう}り: retail — selling in small quantities directly to consumers
